chunks: And ʿAlī ibn al-Nuʿmān narrated from Saʿīd al-Aʿraj, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about a man who has stoned the jamarāt, slaughtered, and shaved his head: may he wear a shirt and a cap before he visits the House? He said, “If he is performing tamattuʿ, then no; and if he is performing ifrād for the hajj, then yes.”

key_terms.الْبَيْتَ: the Sacred House, i.e. the Kaʿbah
key_terms.الْجِمَارَ: the ritual stone-pillars pelted during hajj
key_terms.حَلَقَ: shaved the head as part of pilgrimage rites

ai.seo_question: Can a pilgrim wear a shirt and cap after shaving and slaughtering but before visiting the Kaʿbah?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about what becomes permissible for a pilgrim after stoning, slaughtering, and shaving, but before visiting the Sacred House. It distinguishes between the mutamattiʿ and the mufrid in hajj, ruling that the mufrid may wear sewn clothing at that stage, while the mutamattiʿ may not.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3096 - Ali ibn al-Nu'man narrated from Sa'id al-A'raj, from Abu Abdullah (as), who said:

I asked him about a man who has stoned the pillars, slaughtered his sacrifice, and shaved his head—can he wear a shirt and a cap before visiting the House?
Imam (as) replied: "If he is performing Tamattu' (Hajj combined with Umrah), then no. But if he is performing Ifrad (Hajj alone), then yes."
